title: Replacing an anchored node keeps its anchor, so an alias reads the new value
notes: Replacing the anchored node itself is the way to change a shared value (writing at the anchor's source), and the alias after it now reads null. The anchor stays and the new scalar is separated from it; keeping the anchor is a kit convention. Compare edit/alias-replace-source-of-anchor and the removal refusals, which are about taking the anchor away.

provenance.reference: A writer that put the new scalar directly after the anchor name, so `&s` and `null` became the anchor `&snull` and the alias lost its anchor.
